cues.zh: 这是一期关于延缓衰老速度研究的视频
cues.en: This is a video about research into slowing the rate of aging

cues.zh: 以及延长人类寿命。
cues.en: and extending the human lifespan.

cues.zh: 所以，在拍摄这个视频之前，我想知道：
cues.en: So, before I filmed this I wanted to know:

cues.zh: 你们对这类研究普遍怎么看？
cues.en: What do you guys generally think about such research?

cues.zh: 我发起了一个Twitter投票
cues.en: And I made a Twitter poll

cues.zh: 结果发现，大多数人表示支持，并认为应该有更多这类研究
cues.en: where I found that the majority of people were supportive and thought there should be more of it

cues.zh: 但也有一些重要的担忧，我想在这里先说明一下
cues.en: but there were some important concerns and I want to address those here

cues.zh: 我的意思是，最重大的担忧是：
cues.en: at the beginning. I mean the most significant concern was:

cues.zh: 如果我们寻求延长人类寿命，
cues.en: if we're looking to extend human lifespan,

cues.zh: 这是否只意味着我们将会有更多
cues.en: does that just mean we'll have more

cues.zh: 生病的岁月，躺在床上患上阿尔茨海默病？没人想要那样，这一点我很清楚。
cues.en: sick years where we'll be in bed with Alzheimer's? Nobody wants that, and that was clear to me.

cues.zh: 但我为这个视频采访的教授，David Sinclair教授指出
cues.en: But the professor that I was interviewing for this video, professor David Sinclair, points out

cues.zh: 随着年龄增长，患上可怕疾病的风险，比如糖尿病、癌症、
cues.en: that as you get older the risk of horrible diseases, things like diabetes and cancer,

cues.zh: 关节炎，所有这类疾病……都会呈指数级增加。
cues.en: and arthritis, all those sorts of things... it increases exponentially.

cues.zh: 因此，如果这项研究成功，其核心目标将是
cues.en: And so, if this research is successful the whole point of it will be to

cues.zh: 预防这类疾病的发生。
cues.en: forestall those sorts of diseases.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，如果你真的在应对衰老问题，
cues.en: I mean, if you really are tackling aging,

cues.zh: 那么你也应该看到，那些与年龄相关的疾病不会那么快出现。
cues.en: then you should also see that those age-related diseases do not set in so quickly.

cues.zh: 所以，减缓衰老、延长人类寿命的关键
cues.en: So, the point of slowing aging and extending human lifespan

cues.zh: 在于延长健康寿命，也就是所谓的健康跨度。
cues.en: is to extend the healthy lifespan, also called the health span.

cues.zh: 我看到的其他担忧是人们说：
cues.en: The other concerns I saw were that people were saying:

cues.zh: “嗯，这可能只对富人有用，会加剧不平等”
cues.en: "Well, this could be used only for the wealthy and increase inequality"

cues.zh: 或者“这可能会增加地球人口，导致……”
cues.en: or "It could increase the population of the Earth causing..."

cues.zh: “……更多垃圾、更多二氧化碳。哪里有资源养活所有这些人？”。
cues.en: "...more garbage, more CO2. Where are the resources to feed all these people?".

cues.zh: 我认为这些担忧是合理的，但它们不属于本视频的讨论范围。
cues.en: I think these are valid concerns, but they're not part of the scope of this video.

cues.zh: 所以如果你想在评论中讨论它们，请随意，但本视频的重点是探讨：
cues.en: So if you want to discuss them in the comments, feel free, but the point of this video is to address:

cues.zh: 我们能否减缓人类的衰老？我们能否延长寿命和健康跨度？
cues.en: can we slow aging in humans? Can we extend the lifespan and the health span?

cues.zh: 那是什么样子？我们怎么做？
cues.en: And what does that look like? How do we do it?

cues.zh: 好，为了这个视频我去了“博德加海洋实验室”，
cues.en: Okay. So for this video I traveled up to the 'Bodega Marine Lab',

cues.zh: 它在旧金山北边，我在那里看到了一些“海月水母”。
cues.en: which is north of San Francisco and there I got to see some 'moon jellyfish'.

cues.zh: 这些“海月水母”有意思的地方在于，有些人认为它们是不死的。
cues.en: Now what's fascinating about these 'moon jellyfishes' is that some people consider them immortal.

cues.zh: 怎么可能呢？
cues.en: How can that be?

cues.zh: 这些水母都有复杂的生命周期，
cues.en: So all these jellyfish have this complex life cycle

cues.zh: 它们一开始是水螅体，
cues.en: where they start off as a polyp,

cues.zh: 基本上就像小海葵，然后会经历变态，
cues.en: which is basically like a small sea anemone and then they'll go through a metamorphosis

cues.zh: 变成水母体。我们通常想到水母时，想到的就是水母体阶段。
cues.en: and become a medusa. And the medusa stage is what we generally think of when we think about a jellyfish.

cues.zh: 在大多数这类物种中，水螅体一般能进行无性繁殖，
cues.en: And in most of these species the polyps are generally able to asexually reproduce,

cues.zh: 如果组织被切掉或受损，它们还能再生，
cues.en: and they can regenerate if tissue is cut off of them or if they're damaged,

cues.zh: 而且没有明确的衰老证据，衰老就是生物学老化的术语。
cues.en: and they don't have any clear evidence of senescence, which is the term for biological aging.

cues.zh: 所以它们似乎在一定程度上是不朽的。
cues.en: So they appear to have some degree of immortality.

cues.zh: 直到……我记得是2015年，才有人报告了它们这种能力。
cues.en: No one had reported their ability to do this until... I think this was 2015.

cues.zh: 那么，“月亮水母”是否掌握着延缓衰老、延长寿命的关键？
cues.en: So do 'moon jellyfish' hold the key to slowing aging and extending our lifespan?

cues.zh: 它们能帮我们实现永生吗？
cues.en: Could they help us live forever?

cues.zh: 在开始制作这个视频之前，我会把这类研究归为和下面这种一样的类别：
cues.en: Before I got into making this video, I would have put this sort of research in the same category as

cues.zh: 把你的大脑、你的意识下载到电脑里。比如，我能看出那也许怎么行得通，
cues.en: downloading your brain, your consciousness into a computer. Like, I can see how maybe that would work

cues.zh: 但我不认为我们已经接近那一步了。
cues.en: but I don't think we're anywhere near that.

cues.zh: 因为我们甚至还不理解大脑如何运作，或者记忆如何存储，
cues.en: Because we don't even understand how the brain works or how memories are stored,

cues.zh: 所以那看起来像是硬核科幻，因此
cues.en: so that seems like serious science fiction, so

cues.zh: 我会把比如将人类寿命延长到120岁、150岁甚至更久，归为同一类，
cues.en: I would have put, say, extending the human lifespan to 120, 150, and beyond in the same category,

cues.zh: 但在读了Sinclair教授的书并对他做了采访之后，
cues.en: but after reading professor Sinclair's book and doing an interview with him,

cues.zh: 我觉得这看起来要可能得多，事实上也颇为可行：
cues.en: I think it seems much more possible and in fact plausible

cues.zh: 在我们有生之年，我们会在控制衰老方面取得一些进展。
cues.en: that we'll make some progress over controlling aging in our lifetimes.

cues.zh: 那么，如果你想延缓衰老，首先需要回答的问题是：
cues.en: Now, if you want to slow aging, the first question you need to answer is:

cues.zh: 我们为什么会衰老？我是说，衰老到底是什么？
cues.en: Why do we age in the first place? I mean, what really is aging?

cues.zh: 我以前做过一个关于端粒的视频。
cues.en: I've made a video in the past about telomeres.

cues.zh: 端粒是染色体末端的帽状结构。每次细胞分裂，端粒就会变短一点。
cues.en: These are the end caps on your chromosomes. And every time a cell divides the telomere gets a bit shorter.

cues.zh: 所以人们曾认为
cues.en: So it was thought that these

cues.zh: 端粒就像是鞋带的两端，防止染色体散开。
cues.en: telomeres are kind of like the tips of your shoelaces and they prevent the chromosome from fraying.

cues.zh: 但老年人体内还有其他迹象表明你有老化的细胞。
cues.en: But there are other signs in older bodies that you have old cells.

cues.zh: 有一些物质的积累，它们被称为衰老细胞。
cues.en: There are an accumulation of things, they're called senescent cells.

cues.zh: 它们本质上是这些类似僵尸的细胞，只是继续活在你体内，并使周围的细胞发炎。
cues.en: They're essentially these zombie-like cells that just go on living in your body and inflaming the cells around them.

cues.zh: 细胞间通讯不良，
cues.en: There's poor intercellular communication,

cues.zh: 还有线粒体功能障碍，线粒体是细胞的能量工厂。
cues.en: there's mitochondrial dysfunction, those are the powerhouses of the cell.

cues.zh: 衰老细胞有8到9种不同特征，它们是衰老的标志。
cues.en: There are these 8 or 9 different features of older cells and they are the hallmarks of aging.

cues.zh: 但问题是：它们是衰老的原因，
cues.en: But the question is: are they the cause of aging,

cues.zh: 还是更深层根本原因的结果？
cues.en: or are they kind of the result of a deeper root cause?

cues.zh: 上世纪中叶，当时的假说是
cues.en: In the middle of the last century, the hypothesis was that

cues.zh: 是我们一生中发生的DNA损伤、DNA突变
cues.en: it was damage to our DNA, mutations to our DNA that happened over the course of our lives

cues.zh: 导致我们变老
cues.en: that led us to be older

cues.zh: 但是，
cues.en: But,

cues.zh: 此后的证据表明，事实并非如此。
cues.en: evidence since then has suggested that that is not really the case.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，你可以取一个成年细胞，
cues.en: I mean, you can take an adult cell,

cues.zh: 把它克隆成一个新生物体。
cues.en: and you can clone it into a new organism.

cues.zh: 而这个生物体的寿命似乎与同物种的非克隆生物体差不多。
cues.en: And that organism appears to live about as long as non-cloned organisms of the same species.

cues.zh: 第一只羊，多莉羊，寿命很短。她死得很早。
cues.en: Now, the first sheep, Dolly the sheep, had a short lifespan. She died early.

cues.zh: 但克隆动物；现在你可以克隆猴子，
cues.en: But cloned animals; you can now clone a monkey,

cues.zh: 你可以克隆狗，事实上女演员芭芭拉·史翠珊就克隆了她的狗，
cues.en: you can clone dogs, in fact Barbra Streisand, the actress, she cloned her dogs,

cues.zh: 它们预计能活正常寿命。
cues.en: and they are expected to live a normal lifespan.

cues.zh: 所以这样一来，似乎所有信息仍然都在DNA里。
cues.en: So in that way it seems like all the information is still there in the DNA.

cues.zh: 那么，如果DNA里没有丢失信息，衰老的原因又是什么呢？
cues.en: So if we're not losing information in our DNA then what is the reason for aging?

cues.zh: Sinclair教授怀疑是信息丢失，
cues.en: Well, professor Sinclair suspects that it's a loss of information,

cues.zh: 但不是DNA里的信息，不是基因组里的信息。
cues.en: but not the information in our DNA, in our genome.

cues.zh: 不，Sinclair教授怀疑信息丢失发生在表观基因组里。
cues.en: No, professor Sinclair suspects that the loss of information is in our epigenome.

cues.zh: 那么什么是表观基因组？
cues.en: So what is the epigenome?

cues.zh: 你体内的每个细胞都有相同的DNA，
cues.en: Every cell in your body has the same DNA,

cues.zh: 但不同细胞类型有不同的表观基因组。
cues.en: but, different cell types have different epigenomes.

cues.zh: 它们以不同方式包装DNA，
cues.en: They have different ways of packaging that DNA,

cues.zh: 把很多DNA卷起来，使其不被读取，
cues.en: coiling up, you know, a lot of it so that it's not read,

cues.zh: 同时让某些DNA片段展开，
cues.en: and leaving some parts of the DNA spooled out,

cues.zh: 这样更容易转录、生成蛋白质，维持细胞运转。
cues.en: so it's easier to transcribe and turn into proteins and run that cell.

cues.zh: 所以表观基因组负责
cues.en: So the epigenome is responsible for

cues.zh: 开启或关闭DNA的不同部分。
cues.en: turning on or turning off different parts of the DNA.

cues.zh: 它靠的是一种叫“组蛋白”的蛋白质来实现的
cues.en: The way it does that is with proteins called 'histones'

cues.zh: 本质上，DNA就是缠绕在它上面的，
cues.en: that, essentially, the DNA is wrapped on,

cues.zh: 还有像甲基化这样的东西。
cues.en: and also things like methylation.

cues.zh: 所以，这些化学信号标记会被放置在DNA的特定位置上。
cues.en: So there's these chemical signaling markers which are placed on the DNA in certain positions.

cues.zh: 所以思路是这样的：当你的身体最初形成时，表观基因组就是告诉你的细胞该成为哪种细胞的东西。
cues.en: So the idea is: when your body is first forming, the epigenome is what tells your cells what type of cell to be.

cues.zh: 但随着你变老，
cues.en: But as you get older,

cues.zh: Sinclair教授的假说是，我们在表观基因组中正在丢失信息。
cues.en: professor Sinclair's hypothesis is that we are losing information in the epigenome.

cues.zh: 这很重要，因为如果一个皮肤细胞
cues.en: And that's important because if a skin cell

cues.zh: 需要保持为皮肤细胞，那就是表观基因组的作用。
cues.en: needs to remain a skin cell, that's the epigenome.

cues.zh: 而如果你没有表观基因组，
cues.en: And if you don't have the epigenome

cues.zh: 皮肤细胞就会忘记自己是什么类型的细胞，可能会变成脑细胞，
cues.en: the skin cell will forget what type of cell it is and it might turn into a brain cell,

cues.zh: 这也许没那么糟，但如果你的大脑变成了皮肤细胞
cues.en: which may not be that bad but if your brain turns into a skin cell

cues.zh: 你就有麻烦了，而我认为这很大程度上就是衰老的本质。
cues.en: you've got a problem and I think that's largely what aging is.

cues.zh: 我得说，我肩膀上有些奇怪的毛发斑块，
cues.en: I've gotta say, there's some weird, hair patches, on my shoulder,

cues.zh: 是随着年龄增长出现的。
cues.en: that have happened as I've gotten older.

cues.zh: 那是细胞……出问题了吗？那些本该是皮肤细胞吗？
cues.en: Is that a cell... doing the wrong thing? Are those meant to be skin cells?

cues.zh: 是它们搞砸了，还是这只是……我也说不清。
cues.en: Are they're screwing up or is this just some... I don't know.

cues.zh: 不，不，人老了就会发生些奇怪的事，对吧？你开始在不该长毛的地方长毛：
cues.en: No, no, weird stuff happens when you get older, right? You start to get hair growing where it shouldn't:

cues.zh: 耳朵、鼻子、后背。那就是细胞失去了身份，细胞会说：
cues.en: ears, nose, back. That's cells losing their identity, the cells go:

cues.zh: “我记不得自己该干什么了，我不再读取正确的基因了。”
cues.en: "I can't remember what I'm supposed to do, I'm not reading the right genes anymore."

cues.zh: 那么，这种表观基因组崩溃的关键
cues.en: So, the key to this sort of breakdown in the epigenome

cues.zh: 是DNA损伤吗？
cues.en: is DNA damage?

cues.zh: 是的，所以当你出门晒太阳时，不像今天这样，
cues.en: Yeah, so when you go out in the sun, not like today,

cues.zh: 而是在阳光很强烈的日子，你的染色体会断裂。
cues.en: but on a day where there's a lot of sun, you'll break your chromosomes.

cues.zh: 而细胞为了把染色体重新粘合起来所付出的努力中，
cues.en: And in the effort that the cells go to to stick the chromosome back together,

cues.zh: 注意：DNA并不是随便乱晃的，它实际上是打包好的。细胞必须把它解开，
cues.en: note: the DNA isn't just flailing around, it's actually bundled up. The cell has to unwrap it,

cues.zh: 招募蛋白质来帮忙，
cues.en: recruit proteins to help,

cues.zh: 把它连接起来，然后它们还得回去重置这些结构。
cues.en: join it together, and then they have to go back and reset the structures.

cues.zh: 而表观基因组的这种重置
cues.en: And that resetting of the epigenome

cues.zh: 大约会发生99%。那1%就是衰老过程。
cues.en: happens about 99%. That 1% is the aging process.

cues.zh: 所以随着时间推移，组蛋白没有回到正确的位置，DNA甲基化被加到了不该加的地方。
cues.en: So overtime, histones are not returned to the right places and DNA methylation is added in places where it shouldn't be.

cues.zh: 我们可以读取这种甲基化模式，我能准确说出你多大年纪，甚至你什么时候会死。
cues.en: We can read that methylation pattern and I could tell you how old you are, exactly, and when you're even gonna die.

cues.zh: 你怎么看出来的？
cues.en: How could you tell that?

cues.zh: 嗯，这是个时钟，我们叫它Horvath时钟，以我的好朋友Steve Horvath命名，
cues.en: Well, it's a clock, we call it the Horvath clock named after my good friend Steve Horvath,

cues.zh: 这些在DNA上积累的微小化学物质，就像牙齿上的牙菌斑，
cues.en: and so these little chemicals that accumulate on the DNA like a plaque on the teeth,

cues.zh: 我们可以读取它，你积累得越多，你就越老；从生物学角度来说。
cues.en: we can read that and the more you have, the older you are; biologically.

cues.zh: 所以你可能只有40岁，
cues.en: So you might only be 40,

cues.zh: 你当然比40岁年轻，但你知道，我现在50岁了，
cues.en: you're younger than 40, of course but, you know, I'm 50 now,

cues.zh: 但我的生物学年龄可能是60岁，实际上我确实是。
cues.en: but I might be biologically 60, actually I was.

cues.zh: 我改变了自己的生活，然后检测显示我的生理年龄是31岁。
cues.en: And I changed my life and then the test said I was biologically 31.

cues.zh: 我觉得特别有意思的一点是：你找到了一种让老鼠加速衰老的方法。
cues.en: I mean, one of the things I found really interesting was: you found a way to make mice age faster.

cues.zh: 那你是怎么做到的？
cues.en: So, how did you do that?

cues.zh: 衰老的时钟源于细胞中信息的丢失，
cues.en: Well, the clock of aging is due to the loss of the information in the cell,

cues.zh: 加速它的一种方法就是去破坏染色体。
cues.en: and one way to accelerate that is to go break a chromosome.

cues.zh: 我们没有去晒太阳，而是改造了一只老鼠，让我们可以破坏它的染色体。
cues.en: Instead of going in the sun we engineered a mouse where we could break its chromosomes.

cues.zh: 破坏程度不足以引起突变，细胞会把DNA重新拼好，所以我们没有丢失任何遗传信息。
cues.en: Not enough to cause mutations, the cells put the DNA back together, so we didn't lose any genetic information.

cues.zh: 但如果我们关于“衰老的表观遗传信息理论”是对的，
cues.en: But if we're right about the 'epigenetic information theory of aging',

cues.zh: 那些老鼠就应该变老，而事实正是如此。
cues.en: those mice should get old and that's exactly what happened.

cues.zh: 它毛发灰白，驼背，
cues.en: It's gray, it's got a hunchback,

cues.zh: 它有痴呆，所有器官看起来都老了，
cues.en: it's got dementia, all its organs look old,

cues.zh: 但真正的检验是：“如果我们测量那个DNA时钟会怎样？”也就是我们所说的“DNA甲基化时钟”。
cues.en: but the real test was: "what if we measured that DNA clock?" what we call the 'DNA methylation clock'.

cues.zh: 我们测量后发现，那些小鼠实际上比未接受治疗的小鼠老了50%。
cues.en: And we measured it and those mice were actually 50% older than mice that we didn't treat.

cues.zh: 所以这不仅仅是看起来老的老鼠，那只老鼠确实更老。
cues.en: So that isn't just a mouse that looks old, that mouse literally is older.

cues.zh: 这个假设有趣的地方在于，如果它是真的，
cues.en: What's interesting about this hypothesis is that, if it's true,

cues.zh: 如果表观基因组中积累的噪音确实是导致衰老的原因，
cues.en: if the noise accumulating the epigenome is really what's causing aging,

cues.zh: 那么我们现在就可以采取一些措施
cues.en: well then there are steps we can take right now

cues.zh: 来减缓我们身体的衰老速度，
cues.en: to slow the rate of aging in our bodies,

cues.zh: 通过更好地维护我们的表观基因组。
cues.en: by trying to better maintain our epigenomes.

cues.zh: 那么我们该怎么做呢？
cues.en: So how do we do that?

cues.zh: 有一种理论认为，数十亿年前
cues.en: There's this theory, that billions of years ago

cues.zh: 早期的细菌迈出了重要的进化一步。
cues.en: early bacteria took an important evolutionary step.

cues.zh: 它们实际上发展出了两种不同的生存模式。
cues.en: They actually developed two different modes of living.

cues.zh: 条件好的时候，它们用能量来生长和繁殖。
cues.en: When times were good they used their energy to grow and reproduce.

cues.zh: 但条件艰难时，它们用能量来保护和修复细胞。
cues.en: But when conditions were tough, they used their energy to protect and repair their cells.

cues.zh: 它们进化出了Sinclair教授所说的“长寿基因”。
cues.en: They evolved, what professor Sinclair calls: 'longevity genes'.

cues.zh: 这些由逆境触发的基因会产生酶，这些酶除了别的功能外，还能维护表观基因组。
cues.en: These genes triggered by adversity create enzymes which among other things, maintain the epigenome.

cues.zh: 如今，同样的长寿基因可以在细菌和我们身上找到。
cues.en: And today, those same longevity genes can be found in bacteria, and us.

cues.zh: 我们拥有这些“毒物兴奋响应”基因，或称“长寿基因”，它们存在于我们所有的细胞中，
cues.en: We have these 'hormetic response' genes or 'longevity genes' that are in all of our cells,

cues.zh: 它们能感知我们是否跑了很多、喘不过气或者饿了，
cues.en: and they sense when we've run a lot, we've lost our breath or we're hungry,

cues.zh: 我们有点热，或者有点冷。
cues.en: we are a little bit hot, or a little bit cold.

cues.zh: 这些基因会开启我们对抗衰老的通用防御机制。那是什么呢？
cues.en: These genes are turning on our general defenses against aging. So, what is that?

cues.zh: 我们细胞的部分结构会散架：它们能把它们重新组装起来。
cues.en: So, parts of our cells fall apart: they can put them back together.

cues.zh: 蛋白质会错误折叠：它们能清除掉或者重新折叠好。
cues.en: Proteins misfold: they can get rid of them or put them back together.

cues.zh: 染色体末端会变短：它们能将其延长。
cues.en: The ends of the chromosomes get shorter: they can lengthen them.

cues.zh: 有很多过程在持续进行，但我认为最重要的一个，
cues.en: A lot of processes that go on but one of the most important, I think,

cues.zh: 是维护细胞中的信息，也就是表观遗传信息，
cues.en: is maintaining the information, the epigenetic information in the cell,

cues.zh: 这样我们的细胞才不会忘记该做什么。
cues.en: so that our cells don't forget what to do.

cues.zh: 长寿基因有三种类型。
cues.en: There are three types of longevity gene.

cues.zh: 其中我们研究的一类叫做“sirtuins”，它们控制细胞中的信息。
cues.en: There are the ones we work on called 'sirtuins' and they control the information in the cell.

cues.zh: 事实上，sirtuin 中的“sir”代表“沉默信息调节因子”二号（SIR2）。
cues.en: In fact, 'sir' in sirtuin stands for 'silent information regulator' number two (SIR2).

cues.zh: 还有其他类型。另一组叫做 AMP-kinase 或 AMPK。
cues.en: There are other ones. The other group is called AMP-kinase or AMPK.

cues.zh: 这组基因感知我们摄入了多少能量……主要以糖的形式。
cues.en: This group of genes senses how much energy we're taking in... mostly in the form of sugar.

cues.zh: 第三组叫做 mTOR。
cues.en: And then the third group is called mTOR.

cues.zh: 这些基因控制并响应我们摄入多少氨基酸。
cues.en: And these genes control and respond to how much amino acids we're taking in.

cues.zh: 所以如果你吃一大块牛排，就会有大量氨基酸进入你的身体。
cues.en: So if you eat a giant steak, you've got a lot of amino acids coming into your body.

cues.zh: 这样其实能阻止mTOR沉寂下来，让你更长寿。
cues.en: That'll actually prevent mTOR from hunkering down and keeping you being longer lived.

cues.zh: 小鼠实验确实证实了这一点。
cues.en: So the mouse experiments actually bear this out.

cues.zh: 让小鼠长寿的最好办法，就是减少它进食的时间，
cues.en: The best way to make a mouse live longer is to reduce the amount of time it eats,

cues.zh: 也就是周期性禁食、间歇性禁食，
cues.en: so periodic fasting, intermittent fasting,

cues.zh: 让它保持稍微凉爽一点，
cues.en: to keep it a little bit cool,

cues.zh: 并限制它的氨基酸摄入。
cues.en: and to restrict its amino acids.

cues.zh: 这就是小鼠长寿的秘诀，对猴子也同样成立，
cues.en: That's the recipe for long life for a mouse, and it's true for monkeys as well,

cues.zh: 那些做过热量限制研究的猴子，
cues.en: that have been calorie restricted studies where

cues.zh: 这些猴子15年来吃的食物，比那些想吃就猛吃的猴子要少。
cues.en: these monkeys for 15 years didn't eat as much food as the ones that gorged themselves whenever they wanted.

cues.zh: 它们得到了保护。不只是衰老得更慢。
cues.en: And they were protected. They didn't just age slower.

cues.zh: 它们没那么容易得糖尿病和心脏病，实际上很健康，
cues.en: They didn't get as much diabetes and heart disease, they were actually fit and healthy,

cues.zh: 而对照组想吃多少吃多少，衰老和生病都更快。
cues.en: when the control group, eating whatever they wanted, aged and became sick quicker.

cues.zh: 有些人想通过少吃点，
cues.en: When some people think about eating less,

cues.zh: 比如限制热量来延长寿命。
cues.en: like, calorie restriction as a way to extend their life.

cues.zh: 但这听起来可不是什么愉快的延寿方式。我是说，要长时间挨饿……
cues.en: That doesn't seem like a very pleasant way to extend life. I mean, to be hungry for longer...

cues.zh: 那有没有其他办法……能模拟这种效果？或者仿效一下？
cues.en: So are there other ways to... you know, mimic that effect? Or to simulate that?

cues.zh: 有些分子能激活sirtuin通路，
cues.en: There are these molecules that turn on the sirtuin pathway,

cues.zh: 骗过身体。比如在实验室里，如果我给一些小鼠一种叫“NMN”的分子，
cues.en: and trick the body. And so, for example, in the lab if I give some of our mice a molecule called 'NMN',

cues.zh: 它能提高一种叫“NAD”的化学物质水平，
cues.en: which raises the level of a chemical called 'NAD',

cues.zh: 体内的防御机制就会变得超活跃。
cues.en: you get hyperactive defenses in the body.

cues.zh: 那你给这些……“衰老小鼠”喂了NMN后，观察到了什么？
cues.en: And what did you see in these... 'senescent mice' that you gave NMN to?

cues.zh: 嗯，出了点小状况。我们喂了NMN的小鼠跑得远了50%，
cues.en: Well, we had a bit of an incident. These mice that we gave NMN to ran 50% further,

cues.zh: 但有些跑得太远，连跑步机都跑坏了。
cues.en: but actually some of them ran so far that the machine, the little treadmill, stopped working.

cues.zh: 我们得重新编写软件
cues.en: And we had to reprogram the software

cues.zh: 因为这个程序从没见过能跑三公里以上的老鼠。
cues.en: because this program had never seen a mouse that ran more than three kilometers.

cues.zh: 老鼠跑三公里？
cues.en: Three kilometers for a mouse?

cues.zh: 是老老鼠。它们跑得比年轻老鼠还快。
cues.en: For an old mouse. They outran the young mice.

cues.zh: 那对我们来说就像超级马拉松？
cues.en: And that's like an ultramarathon for us?

cues.zh: 大概相当于让70岁的人跑得比20岁的人更快、更远。
cues.en: That would be probably like taking a 70 year-old and making them run faster than a 20 year-old; further.

cues.zh: 是的，所以这些是超级马拉松选手，
cues.en: Yes, so these are ultra marathoners,

cues.zh: 如果我们对人类也这么做，我想90岁的人也能拿奥运奖牌。
cues.en: and if we did that to humans I imagine you could have 90 year-olds winning Olympic medals.

cues.zh: 总结一下，有六件事你现在就能做，来减缓衰老速度。
cues.en: So to sum up, there are six things that you can do right now to slow the rate of your aging.

cues.zh: 从第零条开始：避免DNA损伤。
cues.en: Starting with zero: avoid DNA damage.

cues.zh: 涂防晒霜，避免X射线之类的。
cues.en: Wear sunscreen, avoid x-rays and all that sort of stuff.

cues.zh: 第一条：少吃。热量限制。
cues.en: Number one: eat less. Caloric restriction.

cues.zh: 第二条：少吃蛋白质，因为你的身体有办法检测你摄入了多少。
cues.en: Number two: eat less protein, because your body has ways of detecting how much of that you're taking in.

cues.zh: 第三：做点运动。“高强度间歇训练”（HIIT）。
cues.en: Number three: do some exercise. 'High-intensity interval training' (HIIT).

cues.zh: 把心率提到85%，让身体感觉像在逃离狮子之类的。
cues.en: Get your heart rate up to 85%, make your body feel like you're running from a lion or something.

cues.zh: 第四：让自己冷得难受，
cues.en: Number four: be uncomfortably cold,

cues.zh: 或者第五：让自己热得难受。
cues.en: or number five: be uncomfortably hot.

cues.zh: 所有这些都会触发身体的“长寿基因”，去维护你的表观基因组。
cues.en: All of these things will trigger your body's 'longevity genes' into maintaining your epigenome.

cues.zh: 进入“修复和保护模式”，而不是“生长和繁殖模式”。你想想这些事，
cues.en: Going into 'repair and protect mode' rather than 'grow and reproduce', and if you think about those things,

cues.zh: 这些通常都是我们不会去做的。
cues.en: those are generally all the things that we don't do.

cues.zh: 但要是减缓衰老对你来说还不够呢？
cues.en: But what if slowing aging isn't enough for you?

cues.zh: 这正是我采访Sinclair教授时出现有趣转折的地方，
cues.en: Well, this is where my interview with professor Sinclair took an interesting turn,

cues.zh: 因为他实际上做过一些逆转衰老的研究。
cues.en: because he's actually done some research on reversing aging.

cues.zh: 那你会怎么做呢？
cues.en: So how would you do that?

cues.zh: 实际上，你需要把表观基因组重置回更早的状态。
cues.en: Well, effectively, you would need to take the epigenome and reset it back to an earlier time.

cues.zh: 但这怎么可能呢？
cues.en: But how is that possible?

cues.zh: 早在2012年，一位名叫Yamanaka的科学家获得了诺贝尔奖，因为他发现了四种因子，
cues.en: Back in 2012, a scientist named Yamanaka received the Nobel Prize for discovering four factors,

cues.zh: 当这些因子通过基因疗法应用于成体细胞时，
cues.en: which when applied in a gene therapy to an adult cell,

cues.zh: 就能把整个表观基因组重置回该细胞处于胚胎时期的状态。
cues.en: would reset the whole epigenome back to how that cell was when it was an embryo.

cues.zh: 这就是所谓的“多能干细胞”。
cues.en: So it is what is called a 'pluripotent stem cell'.

cues.zh: 当然，你不会想把它应用到全身，因为，
cues.en: Now, you wouldn't want to apply that to your entire body because,

cues.zh: 那样你会变成一个巨大的肿瘤，因为你的细胞不知道如何分化。
cues.en: well, then you would turn into a giant tumor because your cells wouldn't know how to differentiate.

cues.zh: 但这确实表明，存在重置表观基因组的方法，
cues.en: But it does suggest that there are ways of resetting your epigenome,

cues.zh: 而这些方法可能是逆转衰老的关键。
cues.en: and they could be the key to reversing aging.

cues.zh: 我们实验室刚刚取得的重大突破，
cues.en: The big breakthrough that we just had in my lab,

cues.zh: 终于，大概一年前左右，
cues.en: finally, you know, about a year or so ago,

cues.zh: 是重新编程了一只老鼠的眼睛。
cues.en: was to reprogram the eye of a mouse.

cues.zh: 我们选择眼睛，是因为眼睛非常难修复，对吧？
cues.en: And the eye, we chose the eye because that's a very hard thing to fix, right?

cues.zh: 如果年纪大了失明，我们认为这是不可逆的，
cues.en: If you go blind when you're older, we think that's a one-way thing,

cues.zh: 视力永远无法恢复，
cues.en: you're never going to recover your vision,

cues.zh: 但我们决定：还是试一试，豁出去了。
cues.en: but we decided: let's try it anyway, let's go for broke.

cues.zh: 于是我们把基因疗法注入老年小鼠的眼睛，
cues.en: So we put our gene therapy in the eye of old mice,

cues.zh: 让它们的视网膜重新变年轻，逆转了视网膜的衰老。
cues.en: turn their retinas to be young again, reversed aging in their retinas.

cues.zh: 那些一岁的小鼠回到了大约两个月大的状态，
cues.en: So those one-year old mice went back to about two months,

cues.zh: 你猜怎么着？那些小鼠又能看见了，就像重新变年轻了一样。
cues.en: And guess what? Those mice could see again, just like they were young again.

cues.zh: 怎么才能重置这些眼细胞，又不至于把它们重置成干细胞呢？
cues.en: How do you reset one of these eye cells without resetting it to just a stem cell?

cues.zh: 我们必须非常小心，不能把这些细胞重置成基本的干细胞，
cues.en: Well, we have to be very careful not to reset these cells to be basically a stem cell,

cues.zh: 否则，我们得到的就不是能看见的小鼠，而是眼后长着巨大肿瘤的小鼠了。
cues.en: otherwise, we wouldn't have mice that can see, we'd have mice with a giant tumor in the back of their eyes.

cues.zh: 我们做了几件事：
cues.en: So what we do is a couple of things:

cues.zh: 我们没有使用获得诺贝尔奖的全部四种重编程因子，只用了三种，
cues.en: we didn't use all of the four reprogramming factors that won the Nobel Prize, we use just three,

cues.zh: 我们去掉了其中一种叫“cMyc”的因子，它会致癌，
cues.en: we leave off one called 'cMyc', which causes cancer,

cues.zh: 这三种因子似乎正好是让眼睛年龄倒退的合适配方，但不会倒退太多。
cues.en: and those three seem to be just the right recipe for taking the age of the eye backwards, but not too far.

cues.zh: 然后，我们做的第二件事是：把它关掉。
cues.en: Then, the second thing we do is: we turn it off.

cues.zh: 我们实际上可以在需要时把这个系统“打开”，然后再“关闭”，
cues.en: We can actually turn this system 'on' when we want, and 'off' again,

cues.zh: 这样就不会让它们的年龄倒退太多。
cues.en: so that we don't take them too far back in age.

cues.zh: 你能对任何细胞都这样做吗？
cues.en: Can you do that with any cell?

cues.zh: 我们认为可以在任何组织里做到这一点。我们现在已经把它用到了整只小鼠身上，那些小鼠都很好。
cues.en: We think we can do this in any tissue. We've now given it to the whole mouse and those mice are fine.

cues.zh: 没有癌症的迹象。它们看起来确实相当健康。
cues.en: No evidence of cancer. They seem to be really quite healthy.

cues.zh: 所以最大的问题是：你能让一只小鼠整个身体大幅倒退，变得完全更年轻吗？
cues.en: So the big question is: can you take a mouse way back, the whole body, and be totally younger?

cues.zh: 也许从两年倒退到两个月。这就是我们现在正在做的。
cues.en: Maybe back from two years, back to two months. And that's what we're doing right now.

cues.zh: 这太令人兴奋了！
cues.en: That's pretty exciting!

cues.zh: 实际上，这兴奋得有点不可思议！
cues.en: It's freakishly exciting, actually!

cues.zh: 我原以为我们只是减缓衰老，现在却在谈论衰老重置。
cues.en: I thought we'd just slow down aging, now we're talking about an aging reset.

cues.zh: 你知道吗？我们只重置过一次眼睛的年龄，
cues.en: You know what? We've only reset the age of the eye once,

cues.zh: 但我们能这样做多少次呢？也许是两次。也许是一百次。
cues.en: But how many times can we do this? Maybe it's twice. Maybe it's a hundred times.

cues.zh: 所以，Sinclair教授声称他的基因疗法逆转了小鼠眼睛的衰老，让它重见光明。
cues.en: So, professor Sinclair claims that his gene therapy reversed aging in the mouse's eye and allowed it to see again.

cues.zh: 但要将基因疗法应用于你数万亿个细胞中的每一个，几乎是不可能的。
cues.en: But applying a gene therapy to every one of your trillion cells is pretty impossible.

cues.zh: 所以，要让这真正奏效并重置整个身体，
cues.en: So in order for this to actually work and reset an entire body,

cues.zh: 你需要另一种方法，而这就是水母登场的地方，
cues.en: you would need another way, and this is where the jellyfish come in,

cues.zh: 因为“海月水母”——成年水母体内的任何细胞实际上都可以被重置
cues.en: because 'moon jellyfish'—any cell in an adult jellyfish can actually be reset

cues.zh: 回到其生命周期的早期阶段。它可以再次变成水螅体。
cues.en: into an earlier stage of its life cycle. It can become a polyp again.

cues.zh: 看来水母确实能激活类似山中因子的东西
cues.en: So it seems like the jellyfish are actually capable of activating something like the Yamanaka factors

cues.zh: 把它们的表观基因组重置到生命更早的阶段。
cues.en: and resetting their epigenomes to an earlier time in their lives.

cues.zh: 如果我们能弄清楚它们是怎么做到的，
cues.en: If we were able to figure out how they do that,

cues.zh: 那也许我们也能对自己的细胞做同样的事。
cues.en: well, then maybe we could do the same with our own cells.

cues.zh: 我们确实有能力重置表观基因组，
cues.en: We do have the ability to reset our epigenomes,

cues.zh: 但通常只在胚胎阶段才会用到，
cues.en: but that is typically only used when we're in the embryonic stage,

cues.zh: 那时我们需要让所有细胞都保持为干细胞。
cues.en: when we need to maintain all our cells as stem cells.

cues.zh: 随着我们变老，大多数哺乳动物包括人类，
cues.en: As we age, most mammals including humans,

cues.zh: 都会随着时间流失干细胞。
cues.en: we lose stem cells over time.

cues.zh: 而我们现有的干细胞也会随着时间变得越来越受限，
cues.en: And the stem cells we do have become more and more restricted over time

cues.zh: 能分化成的细胞类型越来越少。
cues.en: to the types of cells they can make.

cues.zh: 所以如果我们能理解“海月水母”是如何把 presumably 许多不同种类的细胞，
cues.en: So if we can understand how the 'moon jellyfish' can take, presumably, many different kinds of cells,

cues.zh: 逆向转化成再生时所需的细胞，
cues.en: and reverse-engineer them into the cells it needs during regeneration,

cues.zh: 那也许能给我们启发，让我们知道如何在自己身上做到这一点。
cues.en: that might give us an idea of how to do it in ourselves, as well.

cues.zh: 所以，我仍然认为，要逆转整个身体的衰老，我们还有相当长的路要走。
cues.en: So, I still think we're a fair ways off from reversing aging in the entire human body.

cues.zh: 但和Sinclair教授交谈后，我觉得有趣的是，至少有一份路线图。
cues.en: But what I found interesting from talking to professor Sinclair was that there's at least a roadmap.

cues.zh: 至少前方有一条路，你能看到
cues.en: At least a path ahead where you can see

cues.zh: 延缓甚至逆转衰老是有可能的。
cues.en: that it could be possible to slow and even reverse aging.

cues.en: So let's talk about one thing you can do right now to improve your life.
